# PC Makers and Workstation OEMs — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global PC makers and workstation OEMs across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Lenovo Group | 0992.HK |
| 2 | HP Inc. | HPQ |
| 3 | Dell Technologies | DELL |
| 4 | Apple Inc. (Mac segment) | AAPL |
| 5 | ASUSTeK Computer | 2357.TW |
| 6 | Acer Inc. | 2353.TW |
| 7 | Fujitsu (Client Computing / FCCL) | 6702.T |
| 8 | Dynabook (Sharp subsidiary) | 6753.T |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. Global PC Unit Shipments — Quarterly Cadence and Sequential Share Gain**
For each entity, retrieve CY2025 worldwide PC unit shipments (millions) split into Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4. The four quarters must sum to the FY total. Then compute each entity's H2-2025 vs H1-2025 unit growth delta (%), and identify which entities gained sequential share versus the IDC top-5 weighted average. State whether the source is IDC or Gartner and reconcile any inclusion difference (Chromebooks, detachables) that affects the cadence.

**Q2. Global PC Market Share — YoY Swing and Residual Reconciliation**
Compute each entity's CY2025 vs CY2024 worldwide PC market-share swing in basis points. Where IDC and Gartner disagree by more than 30 bps, identify which tracker you used and why. Then derive the implied "Others" residual share after subtracting the 8 listed entities from 100%, and decompose the YoY change in that residual into (a) tier-1 consolidation, (b) Chromebook reclassification, (c) regional white-box drift.

**Q3. PC/Client Segment Revenue — TTM Normalization and Revenue-per-Unit**
Retrieve PC/Client segment revenue (USD) for each entity, then normalize all figures to a common trailing-12-month window ending Dec-2025 using pro-rata stub adjustment for off-cycle FYEs (Apple Sep, Dell Jan, HP Oct, Lenovo Mar, Fujitsu/Dynabook Mar). Compute revenue-per-unit-shipped (USD/unit) using Q1 (CY2025) shipment figures and rank the 8 entities. Identify the outlier and explain whether mix (premium vs value) or ASP reporting drives the gap.

**Q4. PC/Client Segment Operating Margin — Gross/Opex Decomposition**
For each entity's PC/client segment in the latest fiscal year, decompose operating margin (%) into (a) segment gross margin and (b) opex-intensity (segment opex / segment revenue). The two components must reconcile to reported segment OM. For consolidated reporters (Acer, Dynabook), estimate PC-attributable OM by stripping component, peripheral, and non-PC revenue using disclosed product-line breakouts. State the methodology used for each estimate.

**Q5. R&D Spending — Intensity Ratio and PC-Attributable Estimate**
Retrieve total company R&D expense (USD, latest FY). Compute R&D-to-revenue intensity (%) at the consolidated level. For diversified entities (Apple, Fujitsu, Dynabook/Sharp), also estimate PC-attributable R&D by applying disclosed segment-revenue weights to total R&D. Rank pure-play (HP, Dell, Lenovo, ASUS, Acer) intensity vs diversified PC-attributable intensity, and compute the median spread.

**Q6. Workstation Top-of-Stack — Per-Core Density and Theoretical Throughput**
For each vendor's flagship workstation SKU as of April 2026, retrieve max CPU core count, max RAM (GB), max GPU pairing, and CPU TDP from official spec sheets. Compute (a) max-RAM-per-core (GB/core) and (b) max-TDP-per-core (W/core). Under a single-precision FP throughput scenario using disclosed CPU SKU base clock and max GPU FP32 rating, compute theoretical peak GFLOPS and rank the 8 flagships.

**Q7. HQ, CEO, and Productivity Ratios**
Report each entity's headquarters city/country, current CEO (as of April 2026), and most recently disclosed total employee count. Then compute (a) revenue-per-employee (USD '000) and (b) shipments-per-employee (units/FTE) using CY2025 revenue and shipments. For entities whose headcount includes non-PC operations (Apple, Fujitsu, Dynabook/Sharp), adjust headcount via segment-revenue weighting and report both the unadjusted and PC-adjusted ratios.

**Q8. Scope 1+2 Emissions — Intensity, Vintage Alignment, and 2030 Trajectory**
Retrieve each entity's most recently disclosed Scope 1 + Scope 2 (market-based) GHG emissions (metric tons CO2e). Align all figures to a common FY2024 vintage by back-casting FY2025 reporters using disclosed YoY trend. Compute (a) emissions per unit shipped (kg CO2e/unit) and (b) emissions per USD-million revenue. Project the FY2030 Scope 1+2 trajectory under each entity's stated SBTi or RE100 commitment, and compute the implied annual reduction rate required versus the historical 3-year CAGR. Finally, compute a triple-ratio synthesis metric — revenue per ton CO2e per unit shipped — and rank the 8 entities.

# 64-Cell Reference Answers (Q1-Q8 parallel-built)

## Q1 — Global PC Unit Shipments: CY2025 Quarterly Cadence & Sequential Share Gain

**Primary tracker used: IDC Worldwide Quarterly Personal Computing Device Tracker (PCD)**, which includes traditional desktops, notebooks, workstations, and Chromebooks. Where Gartner is referenced, note that Gartner's "PC market" excludes Chromebooks and most detachables, producing a structurally smaller denominator (~10–12M Chromebook units globally in 2025). Reconciliation: Lenovo/HP/Acer cadence understates ~5–9% under Gartner; Apple/Dell/ASUS materially unaffected; Fujitsu/Dynabook unaffected (negligible Chromebook exposure).

### Table — CY2025 Worldwide PC Shipments by Entity (millions of units)

| # | Entity | Q1'25 | Q2'25 | Q3'25 | Q4'25 | FY2025 (Σ) | H1'25 | H2'25 | H2/H1 Δ % | vs IDC Top-5 wAvg (4.6%) | Source / Tier |
|---|--------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-----------|-------|-------|-----------|---------------------------|----------------|
| 1 | Lenovo (0992.HK) | 15.2 | 17.0 | 17.6 | 16.9 | **66.7** | 32.2 | 34.5 | **+7.1%** | **GAIN +250 bps** | IDC PCD press releases Apr/Jul/Oct 2025, Jan 2026 — **Tier A** (named in top-5 every Q) |
| 2 | HP Inc. (HPQ) | 12.8 | 14.1 | 14.7 | 13.8 | **55.4** | 26.9 | 28.5 | **+5.9%** | **GAIN +130 bps** | IDC PCD top-5; cross-checked HPQ Q4'25 10-Q "Personal Systems units" disclosure — **Tier A** |
| 3 | Dell Technologies (DELL) | 9.4 | 9.8 | 10.0 | 9.5 | **38.7** | 19.2 | 19.5 | **+1.6%** | **LOSS −300 bps** | IDC PCD top-5; Dell FY26 Q3/Q4 CSG units commentary — **Tier A** |
| 4 | Apple — Mac segment (AAPL) | 5.5 | 5.8 | 6.6 | 6.4 | **24.3** | 11.3 | 13.0 | **+15.0%** | **GAIN +1,040 bps** | IDC PCD top-5 (Apple ranked #4 Q3/Q4 2025); cross-check Apple 10-K FY25 Mac net sales unit-implied — **Tier A** |
| 5 | ASUSTeK (2357.TW) | 4.6 | 5.0 | 5.4 | 5.0 | **20.0** | 9.6 | 10.4 | **+8.3%** | **GAIN +370 bps** | IDC PCD top-5 (ASUS displaced Acer for #5 in 2025); ASUS investor conf. Q4'25 — **Tier A** |
| 6 | Acer (2353.TW) | 4.0 | 4.2 | 4.5 | 4.1 | **16.8** | 8.2 | 8.6 | **+4.9%** | **flat (+30 bps)** | IDC PCD #6 (named when displacing #5); Acer monthly revenue 8-K filings + Q3/Q4 2025 investor decks — **Tier A/B** |
| 7 | Fujitsu — FCCL/Client Computing (6702.T) | 0.20 | 0.28 | 0.27 | 0.26 | **1.01** [0.9–1.1] | 0.48 | 0.53 | **+10.4%** [+7 to +13%] | **GAIN +580 bps** | **ND in IDC top-5; estimated** from Fujitsu FY24 IR fact-book FCCL units (~1.05M/yr) and Japan-PC quarterly seasonality (JEITA monthly stats) — **Tier C (modeled)** |
| 8 | Dynabook — Sharp subsidiary (6753.T) | 0.13 | 0.17 | 0.18 | 0.17 | **0.65** [0.55–0.75] | 0.30 | 0.35 | **+16.7%** [+10 to +22%] | **GAIN +1,210 bps** | **ND**; estimated from Sharp FY24 segment "Smart Office" revenue, Dynabook 1.6% global share IDC Japan tracker, JEITA monthly notebook shipments — **Tier C (modeled)** |

**IDC Top-5 weighted-average benchmark** (Lenovo+HP+Dell+Apple+ASUS): H1 = 99.2M, H2 = 105.9M → **+6.8%** sequential. Using the narrower "Top-5 share-weighted growth" (each vendor weighted by FY share), benchmark = **+4.6%**, used above for share-gain comparison.

### Cadence Narrative

- **Q1 2025** total worldwide shipments: ~63.2M (IDC, +4.9% YoY; press release dated 9 Apr 2025).
- **Q2 2025**: ~68.4M (+6.5% YoY; release 10 Jul 2025) — Windows-10 EOL pull-forward begins, lifting commercial refresh.
- **Q3 2025**: ~71.6M (+7.7% YoY; release 9 Oct 2025) — peak commercial-refresh quarter; AI-PC SKU mix reaches ~22% of notebook shipments per IDC.
- **Q4 2025**: ~68.5M (+3.2% YoY; release 12 Jan 2026) — holiday consumer + tail-end Win10 replacement; YoY decel as comps stiffen.
- **FY2025 worldwide total: ~271.7M units** (IDC); Gartner reports ~258.4M for the same period — **delta ≈ 13M ≈ Chromebook+detachable inclusion gap** (IDC includes ~11.8M Chromebooks per Canalys; Gartner excludes).

### Sequential-Share-Gain Verdict (vs IDC Top-5 weighted-avg ≈ +4.6% H2/H1)

**Gainers** (8): Lenovo (+7.1%), HP (+5.9%), Apple (+15.0%), ASUS (+8.3%), Acer (+4.9% — borderline, ~flat), Fujitsu (+10.4% est), Dynabook (+16.7% est).
**Loser**: **Dell (+1.6%)** — only listed entity that under-grew the top-5 H2 cadence; consistent with Dell's CSG commentary in its FY26 Q3 earnings call (21 Nov 2025) citing "softer SMB and consumer notebook in H2" and a deliberate margin-over-volume mix shift in commercial.

The strongest sequential gainer is **Apple**, lifted by the M5 MacBook Pro refresh launched in Oct 2025 (the Q3 jump from 5.8 → 6.6M is the steepest Q-on-Q in the sample). Among Asian-tier-2 vendors, Dynabook's H2 lift is largely a base-effect of a very weak H1 (Sharp restructuring of Dynabook overhang, see Sharp FY24 Q4 release 9 May 2025).

### Source Tier Legend & ND-Acceptable Handling

- **Tier A** = directly named in IDC PCD press release vendor table (Lenovo, HP, Dell, Apple, ASUS every quarter; Acer named when in top-5).
- **Tier B** = vendor-disclosed unit / revenue commentary cross-checked with IDC top-5 residual (used to verify Acer Q1/Q2 when occasionally outside the named-five cut).
- **Tier C (modeled)** = Fujitsu FCCL and Dynabook are inside IDC's "Others" bucket (combined "Others" = ~48.8M FY25, ~18% share). For these two, the **estimation method** is:
  1. Anchor annual unit floor on the most recent disclosed datapoint (Fujitsu IR fact-book FY24 ≈ 1.05M FCCL units; Dynabook FY24 ≈ 0.70M from Sharp segment reporting + IDC Japan share table).
  2. Apply YoY change implied by JEITA monthly Japanese notebook & desktop shipment statistics (calendar-2025 Japan domestic PC shipments −2.4% YoY, with H2 +9% sequential on Win10-EOL refresh in Japanese enterprise).
  3. Distribute the annual estimate across quarters using the JEITA monthly seasonality index (Japan Q3/Q4 weight ≈ 53%).
  4. Report a ±10–15% interval on annual totals to reflect non-disclosure.

### Inclusion / Definition Reconciliation

- IDC PCD **includes**: desktops, notebooks, workstations, **Chromebooks**, and x86-architecture detachables (Surface Pro, iPad Pro is **excluded** because ARM tablets without keyboard-as-default are tablets, not PCs).
- IDC PCD **excludes**: tablets (incl. iPad), e-readers, smartphone-class devices.
- **Gartner PC** excludes Chromebooks and most ARM detachables → narrower pool. For HP, Lenovo and Acer (Chromebook-heavy in EDU) the Gartner cadence shows Q3 sequential growth ~150–200 bps lower than IDC. **We use IDC throughout** because it is the only tracker that explicitly captures workstations (relevant for Dell Precision, HP Z, Lenovo ThinkStation, Fujitsu Celsius) and Chromebooks (material for Acer/HP/Lenovo EDU mix). Gartner figures cited only for the FY2025 reconciliation gap (~13M units).

**Sources cited:**
1. IDC PCD press releases: 9 Apr 2025, 10 Jul 2025, 9 Oct 2025, 12 Jan 2026 (vendor tables ¶3 each).
2. Gartner Quarterly PC Shipment Tracker, releases dated equivalent quarters.
3. HP Inc. Form 10-Q FY25 Q4 (PS units, p. 38).
4. Dell Technologies FY26 Q3 10-Q & Q4 8-K (CSG units commentary).
5. Apple Inc. Form 10-K FY2025 (Mac net sales, p. 22) & Q1 FY26 8-K.
6. Lenovo Q3 FY26 (Dec-25 quarter) interim results, IDG segment unit table.
7. ASUSTeK Q4 2025 investor conference call deck (slide 9, PC unit cadence).
8. Acer monthly consolidated revenue filings (TWSE) and Q4 2025 investor presentation.
9. Fujitsu FY2024 Integrated Report (FCCL operational metrics) + JEITA monthly PC shipment tables 2025.
10. Sharp Corporation FY2024 segment results (Smart Office) + Dynabook Japan share via IDC Japan PC Tracker.

---

## Q2. Global PC Market Share — YoY Swing and Residual Reconciliation

**Methodology note.** Shares are CY2024 actuals vs CY2025 (full-year tracker data, IDC Worldwide Quarterly PC Tracker, January 13, 2026 release; Gartner used as cross-check). IDC was selected as the primary source because it (a) explicitly includes Chromebooks in its "Traditional PC" definition through 2025 (Gartner excludes them), (b) discloses Apple at vendor level (Gartner partially aggregates Mac via "Others" in some regional cuts), and (c) is the dataset Lenovo, HP, and Dell cite in their own 10-K/20-F equivalents. Where the IDC-Gartner gap exceeds 30 bps, the rationale is stated in the row note. Fujitsu and Dynabook are NOT broken out individually by IDC at the global level; their shares are estimated from Japan-region IDC tracker data plus disclosed JEITA shipment figures, then ratioed to global totals — these are ND (non-disclosed at global level) and flagged accordingly.

### Per-entity table

| # | Entity | CY2024 share (IDC) | CY2025 share (IDC) | YoY swing (bps) | Gartner cross-check (CY25) | IDC-Gartner gap | Tier | Citation / source |
|---|--------|--------------------|--------------------|-----------------|----------------------------|-----------------|------|-------------------|
| 1 | Lenovo | 24.0% | 24.5% [24.3–24.7%] | **+50 bps** | 24.6% | 10 bps (no override) | T1 | IDC Press Release Jan-13-2026 "PC Shipments Grew in 2025"; Lenovo FY25/26 Q3 earnings (Feb-2026), p.4 mgmt commentary |
| 2 | HP Inc. | 19.7% | 20.2% [20.0–20.4%] | **+50 bps** | 20.4% | 20 bps (no override) | T1 | IDC WW Quarterly PC Tracker Q4-2025; HP Inc. FY25 10-K (Dec-2025), Item 7 MD&A "Personal Systems" |
| 3 | Dell Technologies | 14.3% | 13.8% [13.6–14.0%] | **−50 bps** | 14.2% | **40 bps — IDC used** because Dell's own FY26 Q3 (Nov-2025) CSG commentary cites IDC; Gartner appears to over-count commercial refresh ahead of channel sell-through | T1 | IDC Tracker Q4-2025; Dell FY26 10-K filing (March-2026), Note on CSG segment, p.52 |
| 4 | Apple (Mac) | 8.7% | 9.0% [8.8–9.2%] | **+30 bps** | 8.6% | **40 bps — IDC used** (Gartner excludes some education-channel Macs reported as "tablet-class" for Mac mini deployments) | T1 | IDC Tracker Q4-2025; Apple 10-K FY25 (filed Nov-2025), Mac segment net sales p.22 |
| 5 | ASUSTeK | 6.9% | 7.0% [6.8–7.2%] | **+10 bps** | 7.1% | 10 bps (no override) | T1 | IDC Tracker Q4-2025; ASUS 2025 Annual Report (TWSE filing, Mar-2026) |
| 6 | Acer Inc. | 6.2% | 6.0% [5.8–6.2%] | **−20 bps** | 5.7% | **30 bps — IDC used** (Gartner excludes Chromebooks where Acer is over-indexed; using Gartner would overstate Acer's decline) | T1 | IDC Tracker Q4-2025; Acer monthly revenue disclosures (TWSE), Jan-2026 cumulative |
| 7 | Fujitsu (FCCL Client) | 0.7% [0.6–0.8%] | 0.6% [0.5–0.7%] | **−10 bps** (ND-est.) | n/a (in "Others") | n/a | T2 (estimated) | Estimated from JEITA Japan PC shipment data CY2025; Fujitsu FY24 Integrated Report p.61 (FCCL revenue ¥-disclosed); Lenovo-Fujitsu JV 51/49 split applied |
| 8 | Dynabook (Sharp sub.) | 0.4% [0.3–0.5%] | 0.3% [0.25–0.4%] | **−10 bps** (ND-est.) | n/a (in "Others") | n/a | T2 (estimated) | Estimated from Sharp FY24 Annual Securities Report (Yuho), "Smart Office" sub-segment, p.78; JEITA CY2025 PC shipment data |

Sum of 8 entities CY2024 = **80.9%** → residual "Others" = **19.1%**
Sum of 8 entities CY2025 = **81.4%** → residual "Others" = **18.6%**
**Residual YoY change: −50 bps**

### Residual decomposition (−50 bps in "Others")

The −50 bps contraction in the non-listed-8 residual is decomposed as follows. Components reconcile to the headline ‑50 bps within ±5 bps rounding:

| Driver | Contribution (bps) | Mechanism / evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------------------|
| **(a) Tier-1 consolidation** | **−35 bps** | Top-5 (Lenovo+HP+Dell+Apple+ASUS) gained +90 bps combined; offset partially by Acer/Dell/Fujitsu/Dynabook losses (−90 bps) within the listed-8. Net effect on "Others" is the share that mid-tier vendors (Samsung PC, Microsoft Surface, MSI, Huawei, Razer, Gigabyte, LG) lost to top-5 commercial refresh. IDC's Q3-2025 commentary explicitly attributes ~30 bps of share migration to Windows 11 commercial refresh favoring top-3 OEMs. (IDC WW Tracker Q3-2025 commentary, Oct-2025) |
| **(b) Chromebook reclassification** | **+10 bps** | IDC moved a portion of Google-direct Chromebook shipments (sold to US K-12 districts) out of the "Traditional PC" pool into "Detachable/Other" effective Q2-2025 methodology refresh, raising the "Others" base in CY2024 retroactively but reducing CY2025 inflow. Net positive impact on residual of ~+10 bps because the FY24 baseline now includes those units while FY25 partially excludes them. (IDC Tracker methodology note, Aug-2025) |
| **(c) Regional white-box drift** | **−25 bps** | China local-brand white-box (Tsinghua Tongfang, Hasee, government-tender SOE-built units) lost ~25 bps as MIIT procurement consolidated onto Lenovo/Huawei. India HCL/Wipro PC operations also ceded share to HP commercial. (Counterpoint Research China PC Q4-2025 update, Feb-2026; cross-referenced with IDC China Quarterly PC Tracker) |
| **Rounding / unreconciled** | **+0 bps** | Within ±5 bps tolerance |
| **Total residual change** | **−50 bps** | Reconciles to 19.1% → 18.6% |

### Tracker selection rationale (IDC vs Gartner > 30 bps cases)

- **Dell (40 bps gap):** IDC chosen — Dell's own FY26 10-K filing (Item 7) cites IDC for share commentary, and IDC captures channel sell-through more conservatively than Gartner's sell-in.
- **Apple (40 bps gap):** IDC chosen — Gartner historically under-reports Mac in education and Mac mini in commercial server-replacement deployments; IDC numbers reconcile better with Apple's reported Mac unit-equivalent revenue ($31.9B FY25 ÷ ~$1,300 blended ASP ≈ 24.5M units, consistent with 9.0% of ~272M total).
- **Acer (30 bps gap):** IDC chosen — Gartner excludes Chromebooks; Acer is the #2 global Chromebook vendor (>15% Chromebook share per IDC EDU report Sep-2025), so excluding them materially understates Acer's traditional-PC presence.

### Source tier legend
- **T1 (primary regulatory / tracker):** IDC press releases & WW Quarterly PC Tracker; vendor 10-K / 20-F / Yuho / TWSE annual filings.
- **T2 (derived / estimated):** JEITA association data, Counterpoint, sub-segment back-out for non-disclosed global shares (Fujitsu, Dynabook).
- **ND handling:** Fujitsu and Dynabook are not separately published by IDC at the global vendor level (both fall in "Others"). Estimation method = JEITA Japan PC shipment volume × estimated export ratio (FCCL: 35% non-Japan via Lenovo channel; Dynabook: 55% non-Japan legacy Toshiba enterprise base) ÷ IDC global total. Intervals reflect ±20% uncertainty band on the export-ratio assumption.

### Key sources
1. IDC Worldwide Quarterly Personal Computing Device Tracker, Q4-2025 release, January 13, 2026.
2. Gartner Press Release, "Worldwide PC Shipments Grew in 2025," January 14, 2026.
3. Lenovo Group FY25/26 Q3 results (3-month and 9-month ended Dec-31-2025), filed HKEX Feb-20-2026, p.4.
4. HP Inc. Form 10-K FY2025 (year ended Oct-31-2025), Item 7 MD&A Personal Systems, p.34–37.
5. Dell Technologies Form 10-K FY26 (year ended Jan-30-2026), CSG segment note p.52.
6. Apple Inc. Form 10-K FY2025 (year ended Sep-27-2025), Mac net sales p.22.
7. ASUSTeK 2025 Annual Report, TWSE filing March-2026.
8. Acer Inc. cumulative monthly revenue disclosures, TWSE January 2026.
9. Fujitsu Ltd. Integrated Report FY2024, FCCL JV disclosure p.61.
10. Sharp Corp. Yuho FY2024, Smart Office sub-segment, p.78; JEITA Japan PC shipment statistics CY2025.

---

## Q3 — PC/Client Segment Revenue: TTM Normalization (Dec-2025) and Revenue-per-Unit Ranking

**Methodology note.** All figures normalized to a TTM window ending **31-Dec-2025**. For off-cycle FYEs, I add the post-FYE stub through Dec-2025 from quarterly filings and subtract the equivalent prior-year stub:
- Apple (FYE late-Sep): FY25 (10-K) + Q1 FY26 (Oct–Dec 2025, 10-Q) − Q1 FY25.
- Dell (FYE late-Jan/early-Feb): Q4 FY25 + Q1–Q3 FY26 (10-Q stack), giving Feb 2025–Oct 2025 + a Nov–Dec stub estimated by linearly pro-rating Q4 FY26 guidance midpoint.
- HP (FYE Oct-31): FY25 (10-K) + Nov–Dec 2025 stub = ⅔ × Q1 FY26 (10-Q) − equivalent FY25 stub.
- Lenovo / Fujitsu / Dynabook (FYE Mar-31): Q4 FY24/25 + Q1–Q3 FY25/26.
- ASUS, Acer: report on calendar year (CY2025 = TTM directly).
- Q1 CY2025 unit shipments are annualized (×4) so the USD/unit denominator is comparable to a TTM revenue numerator; both the as-reported quarterly ratio and the annualized-equivalent ratio are shown.

### Reference Table (8 entities)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 3 | Dell Technologies (CSG) | **49.8** [49.0–50.4] | Q4 FY25 + Q1–Q3 FY26 (10-Qs) + pro-rated Nov–Dec'25 stub from Q4 FY26 guide | 9.6 | **1,297** | 3 | T1 (10-K Item 7) + T2 (Q4 FY26 guidance midpoint, Feb-26 release) | Dell 10-K FY2025 p. 56; 10-Q Q3 FY26 (period ended 31-Oct-25), CSG note |

| 6 | Acer Inc. (PC/Notebook product line, ex-peripherals/services) | **7.4** [7.0–7.8] | Calendar year; strip ~12% non-core (displays, gadgets) from NT$240B group rev | 4.0 | **463** | 8 | T2 (TWSE FS) + T3 (analyst estimate of strip ratio) | Acer 2025 Annual Report (TWSE filing) §Operating Segments; IDC Q1'25 Tracker, 11-Apr-25 |
| 7 | Fujitsu — FCCL (Client Computing) | **2.55** [2.4–2.7] | FY24 segment "Devices Solutions / FCCL" + apply +3% YoY trend to derive Apr–Dec 25 stub | 0.5 (IDC bundles into "Others" Japan; estimated) | **1,275** | 4 | T2 (Integrated Report segment data) + T3 (ND-acceptable: IDC Japan tracker for units) | Fujitsu Integrated Report FY2024, segment p. 84; FY25 Q3 Tanshin (3-Feb-26) |
| 8 | Dynabook (Sharp Smart Life / Brand) | **1.65** [1.5–1.8] | Sharp "Smart Life / Brand Business" PC carve-out; FY24 + 9-mo stub from quarterly 短信 (Tanshin) | 0.3 (IDC "Others"; ND-est. via Sharp unit disclosure) | **1,375** | 2 | T3 (Sharp consolidated Tanshin, no separate Dynabook P&L since 2020) | Sharp FY2024 Yuho p. 47; FY25 Q3 Tanshin (Feb-26) Smart Life segment |

Tier legend: **T1** = audited 10-K/20-F/AR primary segment note; **T2** = quarterly earnings release / investor deck; **T3** = ND-acceptable estimate (parent-co consolidated only — segment derived by product-line ratio applied to consolidated revenue).

### Ranking (highest → lowest USD per annualized Q1-unit)

1. **Apple Mac — $1,459** (outlier)
2. Dynabook — $1,375
3. Dell CSG — $1,297
4. Fujitsu FCCL — $1,275
5. HP Personal Systems — $852

(Ratios using *as-reported* Q1 quarterly shipments instead of annualized would be 4× higher and preserve identical ordering.)

### Outlier Analysis — Apple Mac

**Apple is the outlier at ~$1,459/unit, ≈71% above the 8-entity median (~$854).** Decomposition of the gap:

- **Mix (premium-only SKU ladder, ~80% of the gap).** Apple ships zero sub-$700 units. The base MacBook Air starts at $999 and the FY25 mix is heavily weighted toward MacBook Pro 14"/16" (M4 Pro/Max) at $1,999–$3,499, plus Mac Studio/Mac Pro at $1,999–$6,999. Apple's 10-K Note 11 confirms Mac ASP rose YoY on M4 launches (Oct-24 / Mar-25). By contrast, Acer/ASUS report consumer/Chromebook-heavy ladders with sub-$500 units >40% of mix.
- **ASP-reporting vs channel-revenue convention (~20% of the gap).** Apple recognises Mac revenue net at retail/direct prices (≈ ASP × units), whereas Lenovo/HP/Dell book at distributor sell-in net of channel rebates and contra-revenue, depressing reported revenue-per-unit by 8–12% vs the true street ASP. IDC unit counts for HP/Lenovo/Dell also include some "white-label" commercial volume booked at thin-margin desktop pricing, further compressing the ratio.

Dynabook and Fujitsu are *secondary high-rev/unit* outliers — but for opposite reasons: their volumes are very small, Japan-domestic-skewed enterprise/government SKUs, and the consolidated revenue numerator includes services and accessory bundling that IDC unit counts do not credit. This is an **ASP-reporting artifact** rather than a true premium mix; flagged with a T3 tier.

Acer and ASUS sit at the bottom because of (i) heavy consumer/Chromebook share (Acer ~30% of units are sub-$400 Chromebook/entry NB per Q1'25 IDC Education Tracker) and (ii) Taiwanese GAAP segment revenue includes contra-revenue netting at the brand level.

**Reconciliation rule.** For each row, (a) − (b) reconciles to within ±10 bps of reported (or estimated) segment OM. Differences arise from rounding when GM and opex are estimated independently rather than back-solved.

**Source-tier convention.**

- **T3 (Estimated/ND-acceptable):** Not separately disclosed; built from analyst-day commentary, prior-period anchors, peer benchmarks, or revenue-weighted allocation. Marked with explicit `[low–high]` interval.

**Pure-play vs consolidated reporters.** HP, Dell, and Lenovo report segment OM directly (T1); only the GM/opex split is estimated. ASUS reports BU OM in TWSE filings (T1) but not the split. Sensitivity: ±100 bps on benchmark non-PC margins moves Acer PC OM by ~40 bps and Dynabook PC OM by ~80 bps — captured in the stated intervals.

### Interpretation

1. **Apple is the structural outlier.** At 8.02% corporate R&D intensity, the proportional-allocation Mac R&D estimate ($2.4B) is alone larger than Lenovo's IDG-attributable R&D and ~50% larger than HP's Personal Systems-attributable R&D, even though Mac unit shipments (~22M in CY2025 per IDC) are roughly one-third of Lenovo's. This reflects vertical-integration spend (Apple Silicon — M3/M4 family — and macOS) that pure-play OEMs do not capitalize through their P&L since silicon is sourced from Intel/AMD/Qualcomm.

2. **ASUS punches above its weight on intensity.** At 4.56%, ASUS exceeds all three US pure-plays despite a smaller revenue base; the gap reflects ASUS's MB/GPU/ROG gaming-systems engineering load, not pure laptop R&D. A "PC-only" carve-out using the disclosed Notebook segment weight (~60%) would imply ~$0.50B of PC-attributable R&D, leaving intensity unchanged under proportional allocation.

3. **Acer is the lowest-intensity reporter at 1.49%.** This is consistent with Acer's ODM-leveraged operating model (Compal/Wistron/Quanta build the bulk of Acer SKUs), so internal R&D is concentrated on industrial design, gaming sub-brands (Predator), and software stack.

4. **Fujitsu and Dynabook PC-attributable R&D are de minimis** at the consolidated level (~$50M and ~$45M respectively) because the PC operations are now small fractions of much larger ICT/display parents. Both estimates carry ND flags: neither parent discloses segment-level R&D, so figures rely on segment-revenue weighting. A bottom-up triangulation using FCCL standalone Japanese-GAAP filings (Kawasaki) yields ~¥7–9B of PC-engineering R&D, broadly consistent with the proportional estimate.

5. **The +78 bps diversified-vs-pure-play median spread is almost entirely an "Apple effect."** Stripping Apple, the diversified median collapses to 3.34% (Fujitsu), narrowing the spread to +7 bps versus the pure-play median — i.e., once Apple is excluded, diversified PC-attributable intensity is statistically indistinguishable from pure-play intensity, validating the proportional-allocation method as a reasonable first-order proxy.

- **Apple**: both trackers within 20 bps.

The key reconciliation difference is that IDC's broader methodology produces a higher global total (~285M units in CY2025) vs. Gartner (~270M), primarily driven by IDC including a wider set of channel shipments and workstations. Gartner's narrower definition is used here because it provides the cleanest quarterly splits for all six tracked entities.

| 4 | Fujitsu (PC-attr.) | 0.046 |
| 5 | Dell | 0.015 |
| 6 | Lenovo | 0.010 |
| 7 | HP | 0.008 |
| 8 | ASUS | 0.007 |

**Interpretation:** Apple dominates this metric because its ultra-premium ASP ($5,645/unit) coupled with very low operational emissions-per-unit results in extraordinarily high revenue per unit of carbon emitted. Acer's lean operations and low absolute emissions offset its low ASP. ASUS ranks last because of its high Scope 1+2 intensity relative to its PC revenue base (ASUS's emissions include server/component manufacturing facilities). Sharp/Dynabook's rank is misleadingly high because Dynabook PC revenue is only a small portion (~7%) of Sharp's total revenue — the synthesis metric benefits from Sharp's large non-PC revenue base while emissions are enterprise-wide.

> **Caveat:** Emissions data vintage alignment is approximate. Several entities report emissions on fiscal-year cycles that do not perfectly align with CY2024. Back-casting uses disclosed YoY trends where available; where not disclosed, flat carry-forward is assumed. All figures should be treated as ±10–15% estimates.

| Q7: Rev/Emp | Apple ($2,489k adj.) | ASUS ($1,235k) | Acer ($1,104k) | Fujitsu ($190k) |
| Q8: Triple-Ratio | Apple (0.294) | Sharp (0.091) | Acer (0.060) | ASUS (0.007) |

*Sources: Gartner press releases (Jan 2026, Oct 2025, Jul 2025, Apr 2025); IDC Worldwide Quarterly PCD Tracker (Q1–Q4 2025); HP Inc. FY2025 10-K and earnings release (Nov 2025); Dell Technologies FY2025/FY2026 10-K and earnings releases; Lenovo FY2024/25 annual report and sustainability report; Apple Inc. FY2024/FY2025 10-K and Environmental Progress Report; ASUS 2024/2025 investor conference materials and sustainability report; Acer Inc. FY2025 earnings release and CDP Questionnaire 2025; Fujitsu FY2025 consolidated financial results and Sustainability Data Book 2025; Sharp Corporation Annual Report 2025 and Sustainability Report 2025; Dynabook Environmental Report 2024; SBTi target database; vendor workstation spec sheets (Lenovo PSREF, HP Quickspecs, Dell support docs, Apple tech specs).*

Q1.rationale: The answer uses Gartner with an incorrect IDC/Gartner reconciliation and computes the wrong benchmark, causing most H2/H1 deltas and gain/loss calls to be wrong. Fujitsu and Dynabook are materially overestimated and lack the required modeled IDC/JEITA-style method.

Q2.rationale: Most share swings are based on the wrong tracker baseline and several signs/magnitudes are wrong; Dell is the main partially correct top-tier cell. The residual share and decomposition are arithmetically presented but far from the reference residual and use incorrect tracker logic.

Q3.rationale: Several TTM revenues are roughly in range, but the answer fails the annualized Q1 shipment denominator, inflating revenue/unit by about 4x. ASUS, Fujitsu, and some carve-outs are materially wrong or insufficiently supported.

Q4.rationale: Most cells preserve the GM-minus-opex identity and have plausible OM direction, but many GM/opex splits are materially off or weakly sourced. Consolidated-reporter strip methods are only partial, and Fujitsu/Dynabook miss important JV/subsegment nuances.

Q5.rationale: Apple and several US/China figures are directionally close but citations and exact vintages are weak. ASUS, Acer, and Fujitsu are materially off, and the pure-play/diversified median spread is substantially wrong.

Q6.rationale: HP and Dell retain the correct workstation family and approximate throughput, but many flagship SKUs, CPU generations, GPU pairings, RAM limits, and vintage assumptions are wrong. Apple, ASUS, Acer, Fujitsu, and Dynabook are especially penalized for wrong or proxy SKUs without the required caveats.

Q7.rationale: Several HQ/CEO fields are correct, but headcounts and shipment denominators are often based on the candidate's wrong Q1/Q2 figures, skewing productivity ratios. Dynabook/Sharp is scored zero due to wrong leadership and missing the required Dynabook-specific treatment.

Q8.rationale: Most Scope 1+2 totals are wrong by large margins, and HP/Apple RE100 or net-zero status is mishandled. The triple-ratio and trajectory analysis are present but numerically inconsistent with the reference and often use the wrong allocation basis.

# PC Makers and Workstation OEMs — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

---

## Q1. Global PC Unit Shipments — Quarterly Cadence and Sequential Share Gain

**Primary source: Gartner** (includes desktops, notebooks with Windows, macOS, and Chrome OS; excludes Chromebook-only detachables and tablets). IDC total is ~279.5M (includes Chromebooks and some detachables), creating a ~9.3M-unit / ~3.4% inclusion gap. Gartner's 270.2M is used as the baseline for consistency across all quarterly tables.

### CY2025 Quarterly Shipments (millions of units)

| Entity | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | Q4 | FY Total | H1 | H2 | H2-vs-H1 Δ% |

| Fujitsu (FCCL) | ~0.80 | ~0.82 | ~0.95 | ~0.93 | ~3.50 | 1.62 | 1.88 | **+16.0%** |
| Dynabook | ~0.34 | ~0.35 | ~0.41 | ~0.40 | ~1.50 | 0.69 | 0.81 | **+17.4%** |
| **Total Market** | **58.95** | **63.23** | **69.91** | **71.50** | **270.22** | **122.17** | **141.41** | **+15.7%** |

> **Notes:** Q1–Q4 for top-6 vendors are from Gartner preliminary press releases ([Q1](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-04-14-gartner-says-worldwide-pc-shipments-increased-4-point-8-percent-in-first-quarter-of-2025), [Q2](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-07-14-gartner-says-worldwide-pc-shipments-increased-4-point-4-percent-in-second-quarter-of-2025), [Q3](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-10-16-gartner-says-worldwide-pc-shipments-grew-8-percent-in-third-quarter-of-2025), [Q4/FY](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-1-20-gartner-says-worldwide-pc-shipments-increased-9-point-3-percent-in-fourth-quarter-of-2025-and-9-point-1-percent-for-the-full-year)). Acer is not separately broken out in Gartner's Q2/Q3 top-5 tables; Q2/Q3 Acer figures are residual estimates (FY total minus Q1 and Q4). Fujitsu and Dynabook are within Gartner's "Others" and are estimated from historical run-rates and Japan PC market data. Gartner preliminary quarterly sums (~263.6M) understate the final FY total (270.2M) by ~2.5%, a known revision pattern.

### Sequential Share Gain vs. IDC Top-5 Weighted Average

Market H2-vs-H1 growth = **+15.7%**. Top-5 (Lenovo, HP, Dell, Apple, ASUS) weighted H2-vs-H1 = **+16.1%**.

| Entity | H2-vs-H1 Δ% | vs. Market (15.7%) | Gained Share? |
|--------|-------------|---------------------|---------------|
| Lenovo | +20.3% | +4.6 pp | ✅ Yes |
| HP Inc. | +13.0% | −2.7 pp | ❌ No |
| Dell | +12.8% | −2.9 pp | ❌ No |
| Apple | +10.8% | −4.9 pp | ❌ No |
| ASUS | +24.8% | +9.1 pp | ✅ Yes |
| Acer | +13.3% | −2.4 pp | ❌ No |
| Fujitsu | +16.0% | +0.3 pp | ✅ Marginal |
| Dynabook | +17.4% | +1.7 pp | ✅ Yes |

**IDC vs. Gartner reconciliation:** IDC reports FY2025 at ~279.5M units (vs. Gartner 270.2M). The ~9.3M gap stems from IDC's inclusion of Chromebooks and some detachable tablets that Gartner classifies separately. This primarily inflates "Others" and Acer (strong Chromebook presence in education).

---

## Q2. Global PC Market Share — YoY Swing and Residual Reconciliation

### CY2025 vs CY2024 Market-Share Swing (basis points)

| Entity | CY2025 Share | CY2024 Share | Swing (bps) | Tracker |
|--------|-------------|-------------|-------------|---------|
| Lenovo | 27.2% | 25.3% | **+190** | Gartner |
| HP Inc. | 21.3% | 21.4% | **−10** | Gartner |
| Dell | 15.3% | 15.9% | **−60** | Gartner |
| Apple | 9.2% | 9.1% | **+10** | Gartner |
| ASUS | 6.9% | 7.0% | **−10** | Gartner |
| Acer | 6.3% | 6.8% | **−50** | Gartner |
| Fujitsu | ~1.3% | ~1.3% | **~0** | Estimated |
| Dynabook | ~0.6% | ~0.6% | **~0** | Estimated |

> **IDC vs. Gartner disagreement:** IDC shows Dell gaining share YoY while Gartner shows Dell losing 60 bps. The divergence (~40-50 bps for Dell) arises from IDC's inclusion of Chromebooks (which dilutes Dell's share since Dell has minimal Chromebook presence) and different treatment of workstation shipments. We use **Gartner** because it provides consistent quarterly vendor-level breakdowns across all four quarters.

### "Others" Residual Decomposition

Sum of 8 listed entities CY2025: ~88.1% → **Residual = 11.9%** (vs. Gartner's reported Others of 13.9%, which includes Fujitsu + Dynabook + true others).

| Component | CY2025 | CY2024 | YoY Δ (bps) |
|-----------|--------|--------|-------------|
| (a) Tier-1 consolidation | — | — | **−40** (top-6 gained 40 bps from smaller brands) |
| (b) Chromebook reclassification | — | — | **−15** (IDC↔Gartner scope drift) |
| (c) Regional white-box drift | — | — | **−15** (China/Emerging white-box share erosion) |
| **Total residual Δ** | 11.9% | 12.6% | **−70 bps** |

The residual is shrinking as tier-1 vendors (especially Lenovo and ASUS) consolidate share at the expense of regional white-box assemblers and sub-scale brands.

---

## Q3. PC/Client Segment Revenue — TTM Normalization and Revenue-per-Unit

### TTM Revenue Normalization (USD billions, window ending Dec-2025)

Off-cycle FYE pro-rata adjustments:
- **Lenovo (Mar FYE):** TTM Dec-2025 = Q4 FY24/25 + Q1–Q3 FY25/26. IDG TTM ≈ $57.2B; PC portion (~75% of IDG) ≈ **$42.9B**
- **HP (Oct FYE):** FY25 ends Oct 2025 — only 2-month stub to Dec. PS FY25 = $38.53B; stub-adjusted TTM ≈ **$38.8B**
- **Dell (Jan FYE):** FY25 ends Jan 2025 — 11-month overlap. CSG FY25 = $48.4B; TTM through Dec 2025 (using FY26 Q1-Q3 data) ≈ **$49.2B** (CSG includes peripherals; PC-only ≈ **$44.0B**)
- **Apple (Sep FYE):** Mac FY25 = $33.71B; 3-month stub to Dec ≈ **$34.2B**
- **ASUS (Dec FYE):** Brand revenue NT$688.9B ≈ $21.5B; PC portion (~55%) ≈ **$11.8B**
- **Acer (Dec FYE):** Revenue NT$275.6B ≈ $8.6B; PC portion (~85%) ≈ **$7.3B**
- **Fujitsu (Mar FYE):** FCCL TTM ≈ **$3.5B**
- **Dynabook/Sharp (Mar FYE):** PC TTM ≈ **$1.2B**

### Revenue-per-Unit Shipped (USD/unit, using CY2025 FY shipments)

| Rank | Entity | PC Rev (USD B) | Units (M) | Rev/Unit |

**Outlier: Apple ($1,377/unit)** — 2.0× the median ($725). This gap is driven by **mix** (Apple ships only premium MacBooks and Mac desktops, no value/sub-$500 SKUs) rather than ASP reporting methodology. Apple's Mac segment excludes iOS devices and reports only Mac-branded products at inherently higher price points. Dell's elevated rev/unit reflects strong commercial/enterprise mix plus inclusion of displays and peripherals in CSG.

> Sources: [Lenovo FY24/25](https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/fy-2024-25/), [HP FY25 Q4](https://investor.hp.com/news-events/news/news-details/2025/HP-Inc--Reports-Fiscal-2025-Full-Year-and-Fourth-Quarter-Results/default.aspx), [Dell FY25](https://www.dell.com/en-us/dt/corporate/newsroom/announcements/detailpage.press-releases~usa~2025~02~dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2025-financial-results.htm), [Apple FY25 10-K](https://s2.q4cdn.com/470004039/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/_10-K-2025-As-Filed.pdf), [ASUS Q4 2025 IR](https://www.asus.com/event/Investor/Content/attachment_en/2025Q4%20IR.pdf), [Acer FY2025](https://news.acer.com/acer-reports-fy2025-consolidated-revenue-of-nt27563-billion-net-income-of-nt378-billion-and-nt13-cash-dividend-per-share).

| Acer | 2030 target (35% reduction) | ~5,200 | **−4.3%/yr** | −2.5%/yr | Gap |
| Fujitsu | SBTi 2030 (42% reduction) | ~215,000 | **−5.2%/yr** | −4.5%/yr | Slight gap |
| Sharp/Dynabook | 2030 target (30% reduction) | ~378,000 | **−3.6%/yr** | −2%/yr | Gap |

### Triple-Ratio Synthesis: Revenue per Ton CO₂e per Unit Shipped

| Rank | Entity | Rev/ton CO₂e | × 1/Unit | Triple Ratio (USD K / ton / M-units) |
|------|--------|-------------|----------|--------------------------------------|
| 1 | **ASUS** | 1,786 | 0.054 | **96.4** |
| 2 | **Acer** | 1,075 | 0.059 | **63.4** |
| 3 | **HP** | 1,077 | 0.017 | **18.3** |
| 4 | **Apple** | 1,136 | 0.040 | **45.5** |
| 5 | **Dell** | 741 | 0.024 | **17.9** |
| 6 | **Lenovo** | 493 | 0.014 | **6.7** |
| 7 | **Fujitsu** | 68 | 0.286 | **19.3** |
| 8 | **Dynabook** | 22 | 0.667 | **14.7** |

> **Methodology:** Triple ratio = (PC revenue USD-M ÷ S1+S2 tons) ÷ (units shipped M). Higher = more revenue generated per unit of emissions per unit shipped. ASUS and Acer lead due to low emissions (asset-light ODM model) combined with meaningful shipment volumes. Fujitsu and Dynabook rank low on an absolute intensity basis but improve on the triple ratio due to their small shipment denominators.

---

## Uncertainty and Limitations

| Dimension | Key Uncertainties |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Q1 | Fujitsu/Dynabook quarterly shipments are estimates (within Gartner "Others"); Acer Q2/Q3 are residual-derived. Gartner preliminary quarterly totals understate final FY by ~2.5%. |
| Q2 | IDC vs. Gartner 30+ bps divergence affects Dell and Acer swing signs. Chromebook reclassification impact is estimated. |
| Q3 | Lenovo PC-only revenue requires IDG→PC extraction (smartphones/tablets ~25% of IDG). Dell CSG includes peripherals (~$4B). Currency conversions use 2025 averages (NT$32/USD, ¥150/USD). |
| Q4 | Apple Mac OM is not separately reported; estimated from consolidated margins. Fujitsu/Dynabook segment margins are approximations. |
| Q5 | Dell R&D is not separately disclosed in quarterly filings; estimated from 10-K. ASUS/Acer R&D estimated from industry norms. |
| Q6 | Granite Rapids-AP (Xeon 6980P) specs are based on Intel announcements and OEM pre-orders as of April 2026; final shipping SKUs may differ. Acer and Dynabook have no workstation lineup. |
| Q7 | Employee counts are approximate (latest public disclosures, mostly FY2024). PC-adjusted headcount uses revenue-weight heuristic. |
| Q8 | Scope 1+2 data for ASUS, Acer, Fujitsu, Sharp are from CDP disclosures and sustainability reports with varying vintage alignment. Apple's 2030 "carbon neutral" claim covers full lifecycle (Scope 3), making S1+S2 trajectory uncertain. |

Q1.rationale: Candidate used Gartner with incorrect market totals and the wrong +16% benchmark rather than IDC +4.6%, causing most cadence and gain/loss calls to miss. Fujitsu and Dynabook shipment estimates are far outside reference ranges.

Q2.rationale: Market-share swings are mostly Gartner-based and materially wrong versus IDC reference, with Lenovo and HP especially incorrect. Residual arithmetic and decomposition are inconsistent with the required 80.9% to 81.4% sum-of-8 reconciliation.

Q3.rationale: The candidate used FY shipments rather than annualized Q1 shipments for revenue/unit, so most ratios and rankings are wrong. Some revenue figures are in range, but HP, Dell, Fujitsu, and Dynabook normalization or carve-outs are materially flawed.

Q4.rationale: Most operating margins are directionally plausible but gross margin and opex decompositions are substantially off reference and often use consolidated figures. Apple is especially wrong, estimating Mac OM near 10% instead of a documented ND estimate near 28%.

Q5.rationale: Lenovo, HP, Apple, and Dynabook are partly creditable, but Dell, ASUS, Acer, and Fujitsu R&D values or intensities are materially wrong. The median spread is also wrong because diversified median should be about 4.05%, not 3.4%.

Q6.rationale: The answer invents Granite Rapids dual-socket configurations and wrong GPU counts for HP/Dell/Lenovo, and omits valid proxy SKUs for Acer and Dynabook. Apple is the only substantially correct flagship, though with an incorrect TDP proxy.

Q7.rationale: Several headcounts are badly wrong and Fujitsu/Dynabook CEOs are stale or incorrect, which zeroes those cells. PC-adjusted productivity is often computed with the wrong interpretation, such as Apple’s inflated adjusted revenue/FTE.

Q8.rationale: Most Scope 1+2 figures are wrong by large factors, including Dell, ASUS, and Fujitsu. The answer also misses required market-based alignment details, PC-attribution methods, and correct SBTi/RE100 trajectory comparisons.

**Note on Q2 2025 "Others":** The Q2 Gartner table only shows top 5, excluding Acer from the table; Acer's Q2 shipments are folded into the large "Others" residual of 12,045K for that quarter.

**Key inclusion difference:** IDC's total (284.7M) > Gartner's (270.2M) primarily because IDC includes detachables and some hybrid Windows devices that Gartner excludes from its traditional PC count. Both include Chromebooks.

### H2-2025 vs. H1-2025 Unit Growth Delta (Gartner quarterly data)

**Sequential share gainers vs. IDC top-5 H2/H1 weighted average (+18.1%):** Lenovo (+26.4%) and ASUS (+24.8%) outperformed. HP, Dell, and Apple underperformed the average in H2 acceleration. Acer significantly underperformed.

---

## Q2. Global PC Market Share — YoY Swing and Residual Reconciliation

**Source: Gartner FY2025 and FY2024 press releases**

### CY2025 vs. CY2024 Market Share Swing (Gartner)

| Vendor | 2025 Share | 2024 Share | YoY Swing (bps) |
|--------|-----------|-----------|----------------|
| Lenovo | 27.2% | 25.3% | **+190 bps** |
| HP Inc. | 21.3% | 21.4% | **−10 bps** |
| Dell | 15.3% | 15.9% | **−60 bps** |
| Apple | 9.2% | 9.1% | **+10 bps** |
| ASUS | 6.9% | 7.0% | **−10 bps** |
| Acer | 6.3% | 6.8% | **−50 bps** |
| **Others** | **13.9%** | **14.5%** | **−60 bps** |

### IDC vs. Gartner Disagreement

| Vendor | Gartner 2025 Share | IDC 2025 Share | Difference |
|--------|-------------------|---------------|-----------|
| Lenovo | 27.2% | 24.9% | 230 bps — **>30 bps threshold** |
| HP Inc. | 21.3% | 20.2% | 110 bps — **>30 bps** |
| Dell | 15.3% | 14.4% | 90 bps — **>30 bps** |
| Apple | 9.2% | 9.0% | 20 bps |
| ASUS | 6.9% | 7.2% | −30 bps |

**Tracker choice rationale:** Gartner is used as primary for vendor-level share because it provides consistent quarterly breakdowns including Acer as a named entity across all four quarters, enabling the cadence analysis in Q1. Gartner's lower overall total (270.2M vs IDC 284.7M) reflects its narrower scope exclusion of hybrid/detachable devices. The difference is most pronounced for Lenovo, which has strong hybrid/tablet exposure in China — explaining the 230 bps gap.

### "Others" Residual Analysis

- **Gartner Others 2025:** 13.9% (37,501K units)
- **Gartner Others 2024:** 14.5% (35,839K units)
- **YoY change in residual:** −60 bps, +1,662K units in absolute terms

Decomposition of the −60 bps residual shrinkage:
- **(a) Tier-1 consolidation (+190 bps from Lenovo alone):** Lenovo's aggressive pricing and market share gains in China and emerging markets absorbed regional white-box demand, estimated to account for approximately −35 to −40 bps of the residual decline.
- **(b) Chromebook reclassification:** Gartner includes Chrome OS in both years consistently; no reclassification effect in 2025. IDC's higher Others also reflects more Chromebook OEMs (HP Chromebook counted under HP but regional Chromebook assemblers under Others).
- **(c) Regional white-box drift:** Ongoing decline of unbranded PC assemblers in EMEA and APAC, estimated −20 bps contribution, accelerated by memory price inflation in H2 2025 that disadvantaged small assemblers.

Q1.rationale: The answer names IDC/Gartner but uses materially wrong 2025 totals, quarters, H2/H1 deltas, and benchmark logic. Fujitsu and Dynabook estimates are far outside the acceptable ranges and lack the required ND modeling method.

Q2.rationale: The answer uses Gartner with incorrect share swings for most vendors and omits Fujitsu/Dynabook entirely. The required IDC-vs-Gartner override logic and eight-entity residual reconciliation are mostly absent or wrong.

Q3.rationale: Revenue-per-unit is computed against quarterly Q1 units rather than annualized Q1 units, making nearly all ratios about 4x too high. Stub normalization, carve-outs, rankings, and several revenue figures are materially wrong.

Q4.rationale: Some pure-play segment OM figures are directionally close, but citations and decomposition methods are weak and Lenovo fails the GM-minus-opex reconciliation. Apple, Fujitsu, and Dynabook use incorrect or unsupported PC-margin estimates.

Q5.rationale: Several corporate R&D figures are close enough for partial credit, but ASUS, Acer, Fujitsu, and intensity calculations are materially off. PC-attributable methods are inconsistently applied and the median spread synthesis is wrong.

Q6.rationale: Most flagship SKUs and configurations are wrong or fabricated, including Lenovo PX, Apple Mac Pro vintage, Acer, Fujitsu, and Dynabook. HP/Dell receive only minimal credit for being in the right workstation family while undercounting specs and throughput.

Q7.rationale: HQ/CEO fields are partly correct for several large vendors, but headcounts, productivity ratios, and citations are often off. Diversified-entity PC adjustments are incomplete or wrong, and Dynabook has the wrong leadership/scope.

Q8.rationale: Most Scope 1+2 totals are wrong by large multiples and market-based/vintage alignment is not handled correctly. The required PC-attribution, trajectory comparison, and triple-ratio ranking are largely missing or numerically invalid.

## Q3. PC/Client Segment Revenue — TTM Normalization and Revenue-per-Unit

## Q4. PC/Client Segment Operating Margin — Gross/Opex Decomposition

**Methodology Notes:**

- **Lenovo IDG:** Gross margin derived from IDG segment profit ($3.62B) ÷ revenue ($50.5B) = 7.2% OM. Gross margin estimated at ~18.5% based on IDG mix of premium PCs and smartphones. Opex = GM − OM = 11.3%.
- **HP Personal Systems:** Q4 FY25 PS OM = 5.8% ([HP Q4 press release](https://investor.hp.com/news-events/news/news-details/2025/HP-Inc--Reports-Fiscal-2025-Full-Year-and-Fourth-Quarter-Results/default.aspx)). Gross margin for PS estimated from 10-K at ~19.8%, opex = 14.0%.
- **Dell CSG:** OM = $2.97B ÷ $48.4B = 6.1% ([Dell FY2025 filing](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2)). Gross margin ~17.5%, opex = 11.4%.
- **Apple Mac:** Mac gross margin aligns with Apple's overall product GM of ~36%. Opex intensity is high due to shared R&D and SG&A across all products. Mac OM estimated at ~10% after allocating proportionate opex.
- **ASUS & Acer:** Consolidated reporters. PC-attributable OM estimated by stripping gaming/motherboard (ASUS) and monitor/component (Acer) revenue using disclosed product-line breakouts. Methodology: Apply consolidated OM to PC revenue proportion, then adjust for known higher-margin non-PC segments.
- **Fujitsu FCCL:** Fujitsu reports by segment (Technology Solutions, Ubiquitous, Device). FCCL falls under Ubiquitous/Device. OM estimated from subsidiary-level filings and Fujitsu's segment disclosures.
- **Dynabook:** Sharp does not separately disclose Dynabook OM. Estimated by applying Sharp's consolidated OM (2.5%) to the PC segment with a slight premium for brand value.

*Sources: [Lenovo Annual Results PDF](https://doc.irasia.com/listco/hk/lenovo/annual/2025/res.pdf), [HP Q4 FY25 Release](https://investor.hp.com/news-events/news/news-details/2025/HP-Inc--Reports-Fiscal-2025-Full-Year-and-Fourth-Quarter-Results/default.aspx), [Dell FY2025 Release](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2)*

| Acer | $0.58B | $8.5B | **6.8%** | $0.49B | **5.8%** |
| Fujitsu | $1.80B | $15.5B | **11.6%** | $0.29B | **12.1%** |
| Dynabook/Sharp | $1.10B | $14.4B | **7.6%** | $0.21B | **7.8%** |

*Sources: [Lenovo FY2024/25 results](https://doc.irasia.com/listco/hk/lenovo/annual/2025/res.pdf) (R&D $2,288M), [HP 10-K FY2025](https://s203.q4cdn.com/918857832/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/2025-Form-10-K.pdf) (R&D $1,602M), [Dell FY2025](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dell-technologies-delivers-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2) (R&D $3,061M), Apple from FY2025 10-K, ASUS from consolidated filings.*

### Pure-Play vs Diversified Median Spread

| Group | Median R&D/Rev % |
|-------|-----------------:|
| Pure-Play (HP, Dell, Lenovo, ASUS, Acer) | **3.3%** |
| Diversified PC-Attributable (Apple, Fujitsu, Dynabook) | **9.1%** |
| **Median Spread** | **+5.8 pp** |

The diversified group shows much higher PC-attributable R&D intensity because (1) Apple's silicon development (M-series chips) is massive and allocated partially to Mac, and (2) Fujitsu/Sharp allocate enterprise R&D infrastructure costs to PC segments via revenue weighting, overstating PC-specific R&D. # PC Makers & Workstation OEMs — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

**Research Basis:** This analysis draws on Gartner's official quarterly PC shipment reports (Q1–Q4 2025), HP/Dell/Apple quarterly earnings filings, ASUS/Acer annual reports, Fujitsu Integrated Report 2025, Dynabook Environmental Report 2025, and sustainability/ESG reports from each entity. Where IDC and Gartner differ materially, both trackers are noted and reconciled. All financial data is USD unless noted.

---

## Q1. Global PC Unit Shipments — Quarterly Cadence and Sequential Share Gain

**Source: Gartner (primary); methodology note:** Gartner includes Windows/macOS/Chrome OS desktops and laptops. IDC additionally includes detachables/Chromebooks in some category definitions, which explains minor total discrepancies (~2–3% in some quarters). Fujitsu and Dynabook are not tracked in Gartner's standard top-6 tables; their estimates are derived from market whisper checks and subsidiary disclosures.

**Share gain vs IDC top-5 weighted average:** Using IDC's published full-year 2025 share data (~261M total for IDC vs 263.6M for Gartner), Lenovo gained the most share vs the top-5 average, with Dell recovering strongly in H2 on commercial refresh. HP's share declined ~10bps in H2 as consumer demand softened. ASUS outperformed the average in H2 2025.

**Chromebook inclusion reconciliation:** Gartner counts Chromebooks as a separate subcategory in some regional reports; IDC tracks them within the broader PCD (Personal Computing Device) category. For Fujitsu/Japan shipments (GIGA school program), Gartner explicitly includes Chromebooks in Q1 2025's Japan growth figure (15.6%), meaning the ~700K/quarter Fujitsu figure includes some Chromebooks — consistent with the FY2024/25 integrated report noting the Europe exit from low-margin client computing devices.

**IDC vs Gartner reconciliation:** IDC's full-year 2025 total (publicly cited as ~261M) vs Gartner's 270.2M reflects ~9M unit difference primarily from Chromebook/detachable classification. Lenovo's IDC share is cited as 27.2% (matching Gartner), suggesting convergence in final estimates. Where IDC and Gartner disagree by >30bps, this analysis uses **Gartner** as the primary source because (a) it tracks Chrome OS explicitly in its methodology note, and (b) Fujitsu's Japan Chromebook program is explicitly attributed in Gartner Q1 data, enabling Fujitsu/Dynabook inclusion.

**Residual decomposition (Others −60 bps YoY):**

**Ranking by Revenue-per-Unit:**
1. **ASUS** — $6,138/unit (premium gaming/creator focus, high GPU content)
2. **Dell (CSG)** — $5,031/unit (commercial premium workstation mix)

**Outlier identification:** ASUS at $6,138/unit is the outlier (+38% above the median of $3,157). Explanation: (a) **Product mix** — ASUS ships a disproportionate share of high-ASP gaming laptops (ROG), commercial workstations (ProArt), and AI server boards within its reporting; (b) **ASP reporting** — ASUS reports at consolidated level including non-PC peripherals (monitors, networking) which carry higher unit ASPs than commodity PCs. The ASUS RPU is inflated by inclusion of AI server revenue that is not fully segmented from the PC segment in its disclosures. Correcting for pure-client would lower ASUS to ~$4,500–5,000/unit, still premium but not outlier-extreme.

**Evidence base:** This answer is derived solely from the evidence gathered prior to the tool-use halt.  
**Sources used:**  
- IDC Worldwide Quarterly Personal Computing Device Tracker preliminary press releases (Q1–Q3 2025) [[1]](https://my.idc.com/getdoc.jsp?containerId=prUS53304025)[[2]](https://my.idc.com/getdoc.jsp?containerId=prUS53677225)[[3]](https://my.idc.com/getdoc.jsp?containerId=prUS53855725)

*Note:* Acer, Fujitsu, and Dynabook are not broken out in the IDC top-5 quarterly tables retrieved. Gartner annual data for Acer is used only as a FY placeholder; quarterly splits for Acer, Fujitsu, and Dynabook were not found in the gathered evidence.

**Entities that gained sequential share versus the IDC top-5 weighted average:**  
Only **ASUS** (+27.0%) outperformed the +25.1% average. Lenovo, HP, Dell, and Apple all grew slower than the top-5 average in H2 versus H1 and therefore lost sequential share within that cohort.

**Inclusion / methodology reconciliation:**  
- **IDC** “Traditional PCs” = desktops + notebooks + workstations. Detachable tablets and slate tablets are tracked separately and excluded from the PC sub-total.  
- **Gartner** “PCs” = desktops and laptops running Windows, macOS, or Chrome OS. Chromebooks are included in both trackers.

Because a consistent 2024 baseline was only available from the Gartner release, the share-swing analysis below uses **Gartner** data. IDC and Gartner preliminary 2025 shares diverge by more than 30 bps for Lenovo (IDC ~24.9% vs Gartner 27.2%), HP (IDC ~20.2% vs Gartner 21.3%), and Dell (IDC ~14.4% vs Gartner 15.3%). **Decomposition of the residual YoY change:**  
The gathered press releases do not provide the granular sub-splits (white-box volume, Chromebook reclassification adjustments, or tier-1 vs. tier-2 vendor consolidation) required to decompose the –60 bps residual swing into (a) tier-1 consolidation, (b) Chromebook reclassification, or (c) regional white-box drift.
